notes: PRIMARY SOURCES: BLS Table 1502 'Composition of consumer unit' 2024 (single/couple/with-kids/one-parent/empty-nester rows), full URL https://www.bls.gov/cex/tables/calendar-year/mean-item-share-average-standard-error/cu-composition-2024.xlsx; and BLS Table 1300 'Age of reference person' 2024, 65-years-and-older column (retirees_65plus row), full URL https://www.bls.gov/cex/tables/calendar-year/mean-item-share-average-standard-error/reference-person-age-ranges-2024.xlsx. Both retrieved complete via fetch_url server-side rendering (direct curl/wget of BLS xlsx URLs returns an HTML bot-challenge page, not the file). BLS's own consumer-unit-type categories do not exactly match the v2 plan's 7-category household-type selector, so the following MAPPING was applied: 'single_working_age' <- BLS 'Single person and other consumer units' (BLS does not isolate a pure working-age subgroup within singles in these summary tables; blends all ages, so it will skew somewhat older/younger than a strict 25-64 filter -- flagged as an approximation). 'couple_no_kids' <- BLS 'Married couple only' (any age, no children present; some empty-nester couples are also captured here since 'empty_nesters' below uses a different BLS bucket). 'with_kids_under6' and 'with_kids_6to17' <- BLS 'Married couple with children, oldest child under 6' and 'oldest child 6 to 17' respectively. IMPORTANT: BLS splits by AGE OF OLDEST child, not whether the household has any child in a given band -- e.g. a family with a 3-year-old and a 15-year-old appears only in the 'oldest child 6-17' bucket. The v2 plan's 'kids under 12' and 'kids 12-18' buckets do not line up cleanly with BLS's under-6/6-17/18+ breaks: 'with_kids_under6' is a partial proxy for 'kids under 12' (undercounts households whose oldest child is 6-11), and 'with_kids_6to17' spans both the v2 'under 12' and '12-18' buckets. Treat both as approximations pending a custom BLS microdata pull for exact age-band alignment. 'one_parent_with_kids' <- BLS 'One parent, at least one child under 18' (direct match). 'empty_nesters' <- BLS 'Other married couple consumer units' (BLS's residual married-couple category: couples with related persons other than their own children under 18, or with adult children present -- the closest available BLS bucket to 'empty nesters (55+, no dependents)', but not age-filtered by BLS and may include some non-empty-nest households; true empty-nester isolation would require microdata). 'retirees_65plus' <- BLS Table 1300 age-of-reference-person '65 years and older' column (age-based, not employment-based; may include some still-working 65+ reference persons since BLS does not publish a 'no employment income' filter in these summary tables; Table 1300 shows 65+ mean wages/salaries of $23,800 and Social-Security/retirement income of $33,382, confirming a working-retiree mix is included). CATEGORY-LEVEL CAVEATS specific to this file: 'voluntary_savings' for retirees_65plus (2863) is BLS's 'Retirement, pensions, and Social Security' outlay line for the 65+ column -- for this age group the figure mostly reflects a small residual of continued payroll/self-employment tax and/or private pension premiums among still-working or self-employed retirees, NOT net retirement saving (65+ households are typically net decumulators of savings, drawing down assets and receiving Social Security as income rather than contributing to it -- see the same table's 'Sources of pretax income' section showing $33,382 mean Social Security/retirement income received by 65+ households). This line should NOT be interpreted as a 'voluntary savings rate' for retirees without further adjustment in the client-side pipeline. 'housing_owner_share' and 'housing_owner_imputed_rent_estimate' are populated ONLY for retirees_65plus (0.78 homeowner share and $1,798/month * 12 = $21,576/year imputed rent, both directly from Table 1300's 'Housing tenure: Homeowner' percent distribution and 'Estimated monthly rental value of owned home' addendum for the 65+ column) -- these fields are null for the other six household-type rows because Table 1502's captured content in this pull did not include the paired homeownership percent-distribution and imputed-rent addenda rows broken out by composition type; these could be backfilled from a fuller Table 1502 fetch if the frontend requires per-household-type owner shares. CATEGORY MAPPING for housing/food/healthcare/transport_work/communications/education/voluntary_savings construction is otherwise identical to us_ces_2024_by_decile.json (see that file's notes field for full detail): 'housing' = BLS's full Housing major category (shelter + utilities/fuels/public services + household operations + housekeeping supplies + household furnishings & equipment); 'healthcare_oop' = BLS's Healthcare major category (BLS does not separate premiums from true out-of-pocket cost, a known undercount vs BEA PCE per v2-plan.md open question #6); 'transport_work' is a CONSTRUCTED subtotal (vehicle purchases net outlay + gasoline & other fuels + maintenance & repairs + vehicle insurance), excluding public/other transportation, finance charges, and vehicle rental/lease/license fees; 'communications' = BLS 'Telephone services' line only (no separate broadband/internet line in BLS summary tables); 'education' = BLS 'Reading' + BLS 'Education' summed. avg_income_after_tax is null throughout because these BLS composition/age tables report income before taxes only.
